item.title: status site update!
item.description: You may have noticed that something I mentioned at the beginning of the year [1] just became real... Permalinks! Archives! This is feeling a lot like Wordpress wow. :) Sorry to the RSS readers... I know HTML output is still broken. That is still something i'd like to get fixed eventually :[ (... just not right NOW.) Essentially each status update is a bunch of text files, looks basically like what you see here. (If you know Jekyll, Hugo, literally any sane SSG out there, this is analogous to your posts directory with Markdown with YAML frontmatter, except YAML is just RFC-822 headers, and there is no Markdown. (I have an ineffable distain for Markdown/YAML; don't ask me why, but i'm just saying using said SSGs is *NOT* an option for this site even if it'd make my life a million times easier. :>)) Now you may be wondering "well how did HTML output work before", I wrote the HTML output by hand (like `m4 divert' with Template Toolkit conditionals). I have not worked on coming up with a more comfortable DSL for semantic markup, hence the lack of HTML formatting as of late. (That is also out of scope for this "update"...) Anyways, for the longest time, the whole site (with its STAGGERING amount of... 4 files) was just built from scratch, every time. feed.html globs the data/ directory (where I keep said text files), sorts them by date, and includes one's content. (feed.xml does the same except it only looks for specific headers.) This is just a dumb source translation, meaning one input file (the Template Toolkit file with the loop) to one output file (feed.html and feed.xml). To do the same for 47 files (at the time of writing this) would mean 47 sources (!) for each standalone perma- link, which obviously had to be done differently... (But okay, this bit isn't the hard part... you could just, have an actual generic template with substitutable variables. I was just... lazy to write one :P) The harder part is having build those 47 files every time, which is... acceptable given the frequency at which i post? But you know I don't settle for less when I can do better than that... :] I am also VERY impatient waiting for the whole site to re-build when I only changed one single post 6_6 (unrelated to my name but... *ahem*. I just absolutely can't stand being incorrect, to the point my brain would shut down and refuse to collaborate when things are in the wrong state.) So I want dependency graph... but I also don't want magic (black-box in other words, like most SSGs are). But I also want the comfort of not having to worry about things most of the time. You want to know how I did it? Make! or any build system that works on files really. What I made was essentially a build script generator that takes repetitive part out (like writing the file names twice; the `a/%: b/%' that I have used extensively for GNU make). (I wrote it up during the summer in my grandparents' house for my archive project site (www-cellar), inspired by FreeBSD ports I'd been seeing on my T480 (it's a whole-ass language written in Make! I'm not saying GNU Make isn't, but you just can't deny that the `bsd.*.mk' headers aren't totally wack.) The other thing I borrowed from FreeBSD are the /etc/rc.d PROVIDE + REQUIRE headers read by rcorder(8), except I renamed them as HAVE + NEED.) To generalize it to my other sites (including this one) though, I had Claude Code extract the shared bits into a Perl module. So I know, I know, siteconf looks vibe- coded, and it *is*... but it's just the execution and not the idea! >:O And I've accepted that if you want to make something so niche and you need right away, AI is the only realistic way to do it without having me completely give up on college and spend every hour awake to write this. (But okay, on that... I am not getting into that here. =_=) The part I didn't like about GNU make was globbing (which I guess the creator of Ninja also noticed and intentionally left out of their build script DSL.) But, to put it simply, I think globbing is an anti-pattern because if your site loses some posts, you wouldn't know. (The MANIFEST is taken straight from Perl EU:MM, which I like more than how Python and other packagers do it, since I have a clear list of files I can expect to see. (Java is cool though! They have META-INF/MANIFEST.MF :) ) This also helps with deterministic builds, which is something I care deeply about: to be able to know that my web site is self-archiving and not something that needs saving with an external archive system ten years from now. (Of course the checksum on sources and the build outputs and version pinning of the environment will have to be done separately, but the stability of input / output rules won't be a separate concern. ;) But back to this: dependency graph is solved; what's left is just convenience. For that, I just had Claude Code write a source-generator that updates the list of dependencies (the text files NEEDed by a year-feed, a recent post feed, and by the whole site). (Well, I didn't explicitly tell Claude to do that, but it's what I would have done too. I explicitly expected that siteconf would fit in a larger system where its input is also generated. How you generate it is... well, your freedom! Anything that writes to a file; any language. (Same for the build process; you don't need TT, no... a handful of my even older 2024 sites use Jinja2 (back when Python was the only scripting language I knew well enough for something like this...) But there's nothing wrong! Outside of the lack of library function; but then again that is trivial to port... (maybe I will port them when I get involved in Python; or someone else could port it. I don't use any weird proprietary format (though you can't use spaces; that is a serious limitation :c) so the door is open! And i do believe that things will get better from here... v_v)) I am thinking of open-sourcing this site too if any of this is interesting 6_6 But when I'm feeling better lol. (It's unrelated to getting my horrible 2023 sites and maintenance pages archived, no... but more like losing my Ethernet cable, coffee spill on my Mech MX Mini, paid $40 to get diagnostics just to know the soldered switches and the logic board all need to be decontaminated, got scammed $40 from a total stranger said he needed gas to Janesville and he has not repaid me >:c (Think I'm a cash cow for this country or something smh...) so now i am conserving my expenses skipping more meals than i already have been and surviving on fried eggs and scallion pancakes (yes you can get those at Asian supermarkets) and frozen food... not because i need it but because i am just super salty the money that could have contributed to getting my keyboard cleaned, my 7yo macbook's battery replaced, the lopsided Enter key on my T480s replaced went to some jack- ass who thought i was free money... and what, it probably doesn't even cost that much for a gas refill? And even if it did saying you'd repay and end up not actually repaying is just gross. Like how do you expect me to document this transaction on my ledger.... fucking charity??? Anyways.. oh something quick now: there are a few more subdomains you may or may not have noticed? Those are legit -- their sources are all on GitHub; they themselves are GitHub pages like foss.rapidcow.org. I don't like... host infrastructure now? (Except for git.rapidcow.org, but as my git server and not as GitWeb, like Gitea/Forgejo or whatever crazy web daemon they have now. (They also horrendously mutate the Git hooks which I need very badly for audit logs as distributed Git refs.) And www since I need CGI and tilde directories, but well... (but i can't WAIT to get the .com guy off of my site. It is SALIVATING the sheer thought of getting that stink off of me. uwu)) If GitHub Pages is good enough for OpenZFS, and I open- source my stuff anyways (it's also for a free back up, in the catastrophic event that all my existing storage die in some horrendous event... (it's what Linus said was his backup strategy in the Linus Tech Tips video too and I very much concur with that XD Abstinence from GitHub as a gesture against Microsoft and AI doesn't buy you anything. I think private infrastructure should just stay private... no need to announce to the world "I am self-hosted" because, becoming your own SaSS provider is ultimately not addressing the maintainability and sustain- ability of the SaSS model? (I think I said about this somewhere regarding why I don't consider Mastodon to be a solution to the self-indulgent culture on Twitter. Maybe foss? Man I need a proper blog...))) And because they are on GitHub, obviously I won't report "status" updates on those. :) But that's a good thing... it means I can care about different things like contents of my writing (like right now!); and I also get things for free, like... the source distribution part. Disaster recovery, if someone wants to archive it if I disappear... When I feel more comfortable this status page can also go on GitHub Pages! The tools are there anyways. :) (I do especially adore Git as a publishing medium to be clear. I don't like the culture around GitHub but Git is so un- apologetically replicable and decentralized, that you have to both simultaneously love that you will never be locked out of your data... and live with the horrifying fact that any one with access to it basically has everything you've ever written. And it suddenly... oh gosh. (Yeah... it's why I need some more time to process. Maybe next year :D)) [1]: https://status.rapidcow.org/feed/2026/1772459792.html

item.title: ???? outage from before
item.description:
None of this is "public service" but I'd still mention a bit about what I know... a lot of hectic things happened following my flight, among node health features I didn't get to implement...
www-auth was offline but recently brought back. I forgot to upgrade the zfs kernel module with the kernel so, lesson learned from that... (zfs-utils and zfs-dkms are recent enough to support my current kernel version, fortunately. :)
The ns1 HTTP cert expired. I'll look into that. For resolvers out there though, UDP port 53 should still work as you would expect. (DoH has never been public service, btw.... but since i have (am? was?) advertised HTTPS capabilities i thought i'd mention.
(The cert expiring alone isn't worrying; though i would have to check if something went wrong with certbot that could mean similar certs expiring for my other domains...)
The domain/ route (if anybody knows... sorry Mike :c) will remain until I can bring the Pi online by configuring the network with HDMI video output.
Finally I have no idea what happened between then and now on this domain (status.rapidcow.org). I was going to investigate by logging into Cloudflare just now but... by the time I did that it was back up. (I don't really control the "status" A/AAAA records, since it's Cloudflare Pages and all... only Cloudflare knows what happens (besides myself, since i was the only person i know who was affected by this... but i didn't keep any diagnostics, so... that makes it a nobody-knows situation i guess. :x)
rapidcow.org and friends currently hosted on the Ubuntu nyc droplet should be working just fine though. I realized i needed to do a little more "magic" than a simple proxy_pass and auth_request... until i get to do that i shouldn't be touching the sites much. (nor updating them, but you already know how little updates there have been... :)

item.title: Re: AI for code
item.description:
Hey so I woke up today and decided that I *still* didn't like having AI-generated code authored under my name. So I rebased and split out that hunk specifically to attribute Claude, and extracted the relevant transcript with Claude in the commit notes.
It was an exercise in using jq without consulting AI to do a quick-and-dirty job... but it is one that is worth it I think. :) In any case, "git blame" on xlib/tree-search.pl is not as misleading as it used to be. and i feel much more confident writing code!

item.title: AI for code
item.description:
I have been using AI (Claude Code, namely) to write code, and while nobody has mentioned this point to me (yet), I ... still feel like I should say something.
(Like doing a press release, ugh.... but if i don't say something, i can't sleep with this.)
Basically, I don't think i can make a stance that i can stick to. I am neither refraining from all AI-generated writing/code nor embracing it fully. One thing I can take a strong stance against is the so-called AI-generated art; but that isn't to say I automatically like any art that isn't AI. (It never has been the case, so why should it be now?)
Another thing I can say is privacy: AI for my public code is alright, private code sometimes (it's not like I keep my diaries there), but data is where I draw the line. I periodically clean up GPT and Claude's memory because I reveal too much, sometimes... it's mostly my real domain name I forget to deface, but I still prune them regularly to at least make an effort in obscuring my identity.
A third line I can draw is quality: now that I am writing up a patch for Perl; you bet I will thoroughly compare Claude's analysis with real code and my rudimentary compiler knowledge. That also isn't worth a separate blog, I just realized... I'll let the GitHub bugtracking system speak for itself; anything I can't speak directly in front of the developers is probably not worth letting the rest of the world either. (Partially because I am still disgusted by that OCaml pull request; something like https://github.com/Perl/perl5/pull/24402 in comparison at least feels more modest and accountable for when AI "goes wrong".) But like in terms of copyright, yes, I will make sure it's not a blatant rip-off; and if I treat authorship more like "person to hold accountable" (rather than my usual Git metadata model which is to use the author identity as the physical machine used to change the files (and the committer as the machine used to commit it, if that's different)), then yes, I will put my name under it, not because I treat AI code as mine, but because AI cannot be held accountable, and people can't email <claude@anthropic.com> and ask about rationales for the change (not like it even "remembers" writing that.)
It's probably just me but I hate it when I am told on the one hand to do it the hard way, and on the other succumb to AI. Like computer science is pointless, and the job market likes AI-first candidate. Point is I am already using AI, not because I am told one way or another; or that it means I take a stance for or against AI, about water usage, cooling, electricity whatnot, yada yada.... It just means I find it suitable for what I want: getting information fast. Often weird niche information people don't ask about, like... running Nginx to proxy DoH from BIND 9 for my nameservers. (Like BIND 9 has zero concepts of virtual hosts; I had to use two loopback addresses and enforce ACL on that); or my super niche Git server that needs to have directories and fine-grained ACLs on ref namespaces, and audit logs, that I can absolutely ask no one about because nobody is this insane to track everything in a Git repository! And what made you think I am a developer or in all this thing because i care about the industry? computer isn't what i love; art is! And I also like the way programming lets me express what I want. It's one of those things that, once you discover software is made by people, you can't stop thinking about how they could have been made differently... but that's that! I want to make things WORK and not suck, and -- if I am in the mood to -- explain how those work. And if AI helps in the process of making it work, I'll accept it. And in return, if AI inspired an idea, I'll put a short "thanks" below it. If AI generated the code entirely, I'd let the AI proudly put the model name in the author header than hide it in a Co-Authored-By field or any non-machine-parseable format. But I won't look at the AI-generated code, run around and panic "what will people THINK about ME?!" and decide to start over again -- for what? Just because I can't be seen walking around with less than 100% of original thoughts? In my OWN code?
Of course, I won't get to do this when it's someone else's project, and the stakes are high; and rightfully so... This is what I will have to do for Perl 5. I will also not do it when it's clear that this is copyrighted code... (but I would argue that's what git log is for; you would already be able to tell, most of the time, if Claude generated the code or i did. (There is just a tiny exception where I copied the code straight from Claude Code in commit 3625a59; but even then, it is somewhat based on my past projects so *technically*, it's like generated on the basis of my own code... which I DID write! Morally speaking it wasn't that much worse than collocating information (and frankly if we spend here all day analyzing on a per-case basis whether something counts as potential copyright infringement.... Well. :x))
You can see how this is exhausting right? I try my best to be transparent about this, but at the end of the day I just want it to work. And by the time I am done with it, i can get back to my websites, or whatever other archive / homenet project I have going on beyond your sights on the Internet...
(Also please don't post this on HN if anyone even reads this ... I'm only doing this to alleviate my guilt. I DON'T need more judgment than I already do judging myself and analyzing the ways this could go wrong and how I will deal with it. Writing code and wanting to share it with people shouldn't demand a whole lawyer's worth of knowledge... and I should be allowed to have a life outside of all this while having a voice of sorts to change things in a project that I would otherwise have not deserved to make changes in... and still not being the best of best at it. I try to understand and follow all the guidelines and feedback, and not waste anyone's time; in return I just want peace when it's my own code....)

item.title: half-broken DNSSEC rapidcow.net
item.description:
Hey y'all, so I'm trying out free secondary servers to serve alongside my two measly Digital Ocean droplets. rapidcow.net is the "lab rat" this time (which most of you shouldn't know of; i only got it in a fit of anger towards GoDaddy holding rapidcow.com hostage for some unholy cost). currently trying out BuddyNS (which i keep misspelling as "bundy"...); apparently out of all records in the world they don't support RRSIG!
Because DNSSEC is a paid feature? I mean I'd get it if they're the one rotating the keys and signing them, but if I'm just letting you serve the RRSIG/NSEC3... it shouldn't be any more work than being a RFC-compliant secondary server. :(
Ironically directly below a retweet by Bundy^W BUDDY, sorry, NS, the same person says:
https://twitter.com/jefhar70/status/1583566517429338112
> Actually I'm switching secondary dns from BuddyNS to > http://dns.he.net. One of them strips dnssec records > from the slave zone, and the other preserves them.
https://twitter.com/jefhar70/status/1583596812585209856
> Well, they won't strip the dnssec records if you pay > them, but that's like paying for a TLS certificate in > the age of Let's Encrypt.
(I actually removed mentions of BuddyNS and letsencrypt because i hate handle-centric internet. That said, there is a certain tinge of hope when there wasn't a handle for he.net...)
Anyways, I'm dropping Buddy from the registry NS... it's a good thing all the big recursive name servers (1.1.1.1, 8.8.8.8, 9.9.9.9) didn't drop my name records because of Buddy misbehaving... so much for that. >n>

item.title: Too many sites on Cloudflare
item.author: ????? at rapidcow dot org
item.description:
(not typing out my email per usual since urm... spam. (infrequent, but still spam.)
also, i don't believe anyone will actually email me.)
NS endfindme.com now goes on Cloudflare too; before it was Porkbun (though I *think* if knowledge serves me right, Porkbun uses Cloudflare in the background too.)
The reason: serve that rotten clubradar project I've never had any interest in as a PERMANENT redirect, without costing a dime from my pocket! I've heard of good things about Cloudflare Worker from a guy who's been running our university's last and only web-development club (well, maybe a bit excessive of an endorsement, considering the whole CLUB's infrastructure runs on Cloudflare: from registrar and DNS to website and business logic code...), so I decided to give it a shot.
(Funny sorry, following incidence of our university's canvas.wisc.edu being caught in the middle of the (at the very least second) cyberattack against Instructure, our DoIT imprudently used 301 instead of 302 or 307 to steer naive people away from canvas.wisc.edu to alerts.wisc.edu. Days later (the following Tuesday, which is to say the Tuesday this week) someone in the UW-Madison Weixin group chat said their browser just insisted on following that redirect and won't go back to Canvas after it got fixed. Somebody suggested the guy to ditch their browser session entirely because DoIT essentially "poisoned" the redirect cache. XD So much for "protecting" the students...)
So yes, the PERMANENT part is very much intentional, in that I am "intentionally" poisoning any of my pesky teammates who cared enough to revisit for whatever reason. Say that delivers a final goodbye kiss to them for the unsightly irresponsibility.
But there is a catch with Cloudflare Worker ... to get the vanity domain working AND to refrain from paying a dime, where money lacks well your dignity makes up for. Cloudflare wants to manage my whole zone for me with what's called their "Full DNS Setup". Without it you either just can't use their service with your domain (not even CNAME to the worker.dev dynamic domain name!); or you'd be paying them a fortune for a business plan for a "Partial DNS Setup". All for the basic dignity to use a custom domain name.
..... *tsk* I sure do like it when people frame it that way. "Custom"... name. I mean it's your choice to make; sure. You own the network; I don't. I just hate the way it is phrased... as if we regular people owning a little place on the Internet was the exception rather than the norm. Decentralized communication *was* the norm, pumpkin head! When the world was full of small sites and providers respected our personal space like Geocities... and you want to call FAANG and mega-apps like Tencent Weixin the f-kn' norm.
Right now I've switched most of my *.net domains away from Cloudflare; the ones that I am serious about using internally at least. I am going to try to find a balance with things, but essentially... I don't want to grow reliant on Cloudflare. Not while I still have to delete all my name records to upload a new one from my locally-managed BIND zone files (that is currently the only reason keeping me from moving to something that feels more "ethical", like deSEC.io); not while it randomly rejects my OPENPGPKEY record for random errors (and I mean random in a very literal sense -- you literally can't make out s**t from it); and not while, unlike Netlify or Vercel, it refuses to deploy my stuff to my domain because it couldn't accept not having control over my entire zone and have me jump through fancy interfaces just to do the most simple basic task; just minding my own business with my DNS records. Not while it asks to bind itself to parts of my infrastructure more than what I ask it to bind to.

item.title: ns2 nameserver oddity
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
For a bit (I'm not sure how long? Maybe following my futile attempt to move my Tailscale provider to OIDC) ns2 (nominally ns2.rapidcow.net) hasn't been serving any DNS records, and my Tailscale ACL is to blame...
After a re-auth the ubuntu (ns1) server was untagged, which my ACL would not allow ns2 connecting to for the zone transfer. (Normally untagged machines are my laptops and phones, so just imagine mistaking a VPS for that!)
Also, I'm gonna need to find a way to not display the webmaster address directly, since (apparently) bots have found this address and have been taking ample pleasure in spamming my inbox with it...
(I won't be gone for long this time. :)

item.title: Re: dhl.com IN ANY
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
I experimented with my BIND server a bit and it appears that "minimal-any" only applies to UDP replies (which would be the more common vector of amplication attacks?) Namely I can get all the record types just fine with TCP, but that wouldn't be something I can disable without modifying the source code of BIND9 and recompiling it...
Also I do intend to un-privatize the source code of this site; it likely doesn't cost a lot of bandwidth to host anyways. But you do have to get it from me, and not any major Git providers (that excludes SourceHut itself); I just don't want people who don't care about all this find out about it through wicked SEO stuff and "complain" about why it's made of sticks and duct tapes ^^;
(That has arguably been my primary concern with getting archived and indexed and all that... there's nothing "proprietary" about what I know, and gate-keeping for anything more than the purpose of basic protection against attackers, but I would prefer some personal space and "privacy". Frankly I don't like the means I use to achieve that; it is antithetical to all the causes I care about. But just because big greedy corpos with their NDAs like to keep their code industry secret, doesn't mean me as one measly person should open up every code I ever write. I don't owe people anything because of them; and the last thing they can do for me in return is to respect *my* choice over what to publish and what not to publish.)
In any case, I'm open to e-mails from REAL people who REALLY care! (That's why I leave it at the top of every message, anyways! I'm naive and young and still don't know the perils of talking to strangers on the Internet and the risks of getting socially-engineered to do something that results in one of the most devastating supply-chain attacks in all of the history of Linux infrastructure :^) (Surely you must have figured out that I was specifically referring to Lasse Colin's xz being used as a vector for installing an SSH backdoor, well... he's a nice guy, but I surely wouldn't email him about it, since his software is used by millions around the world. On the other hand, you *can* e-mail me, but if I get to that level of "fame" and suddenly say you *can't*... I hope you understand. ;c)

(I should be paying more attention in my R class, oh well. Tidyverse sounds like something that would be very appropriate for this occasion.)
Just now I re-ran the command (that I shamefully have the only copy of in Claude) on March 19 (2026-03-19T22:16:33.907407Z to be specific) that produces a histogram of dhl.com IN ANY requests made per hour, scaled down by a factor of 5000:
# perl -ne 'next unless /dhl.com IN ANY/; if (my ($D,$H) = /(\d{,2})-Mar-2026 (\d{,2})/) { $Bin{"Mar-$D $H:00"}++ } else { die }; END { foreach (sort { $a cmp $b } keys %Bin) { printf "%s %s\n", $_, "=" x int($Bin{$_} / 5000.0) } }' /var/log/bind/queries* Mar-17 16:00 ======================================== Mar-17 17:00 ========================================= Mar-17 18:00 ========================================== Mar-17 19:00 ========================================== Mar-17 20:00 ========================================== Mar-17 21:00 ========================================= Mar-17 22:00 ========================================== Mar-17 23:00 ========================================== Mar-18 00:00 ========================================== Mar-18 01:00 ========================================== Mar-18 02:00 ========================================= Mar-18 03:00 ========================================== Mar-18 04:00 ========================================== Mar-18 05:00 ========================================== Mar-18 06:00 ========================================= Mar-18 07:00 ========================================== Mar-18 08:00 ========================================== Mar-18 09:00 ========================================== Mar-18 10:00 ========================================== Mar-18 11:00 ============================ Mar-18 12:00 =================== Mar-18 13:00 =================== Mar-18 14:00 =================== Mar-18 15:00 =================== Mar-18 16:00 ========== Mar-21 16:00 Mar-22 16:00 Mar-24 18:00 ========= Mar-24 19:00 ================================================================== Mar-25 20:00 ================================= Mar-25 21:00 ==============================

They appear to come from Brazillian ISPs. I say "appear" because... I googled it, thinking it was going to be like one of those crappy crawlers that click on every link (for instance recently I read about <https://zadzmo.org/blog/posts/2025/1218-Thinkbot.md> <https://boston.conman.org/2025/08/21.1>) But the truth is MY SERVER may have been used to attack them instead. Basically, post and relevant reply:
<https://www.reddit.com/r/sysadmin/comments/1r8m3oq/> <https://www.reddit.com/r/sysadmin/comments/1r8m3oq/comment/o6f07ty/>
(This case of that is definitely different in that these "dhl.com IN ANY" requests are made over UDP (EDNS0, to be exact); but the general premise is there.)
And a lot more when I google "reflection attack" (not so much "amplification" though):
<https://www.netscout.com/what-is-ddos/what-is-reflection-amplification-attack> <https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-best-practices-ddos-resiliency/udp-reflection-attacks.html> <https://www.cloudflare.com/learning/ddos/dns-amplification-ddos-attack/> <https://security.stackexchange.com/a/181123> <https://security.stackexchange.com/a/94270> <https://www.imperva.com/learn/ddos/dns-amplification/>
So the flow of such an attack goes like this:
* Botnet sends a plausible UDP packet, saying "I want *every* record---A, AAAA, TXT, and all that---at the name dhl.com.", to a DNS resolver, and forges a source address pointing to one of the addresses of Brazillian ISP. (That is VPSes, but possibly residential IP too.)
* The DNS resolver says "ok" and sends back to the forged address, with kilobytes of (unsolicited) UDP packet.
* Do this many many times, appearing as many many Brazillian IPs. Each DNS request is 40-80 bytes (source: claude; I don't really know how large a DNS packet is lol, it's less than 256 for sure), but the response gets amplified to 2-6 kilobytes. Maximal damage for minimal effort!
Wikipedia has a neat diagram for it (although the gray mess representing "the Internet" is kind of funny, lol): <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IP_address_spoofing>
(Although, now that I checked against my own recursive resolvers, the TCP "rcvd" size is between 6888 and 6063, which are both too big for BIND9's default max-udp-size and edns-udp-size, so it doesn't matter how large the attacker advertises their +bufsize in EDNS (even if they crank it all the way up to the theoretical maximum UDP size of "65535"!). In practice UDP is a dead-end; though they may succeed with TCP.)
But in a sense I can't do anything about it: block these AS ranges and it would have achieved one possible intent of these attackers: cripple Internet service for Brazillian residents. Such an attack leaves no trace either, because IP/UDP/TCP is like, a very low level protocol... (the fact that these packets even got far is a different concern though; suffice it to say though when my server receives them it is indisginguishable from a legitimiate DNS query, albeit suspicious, most obviously to me because of dhl.com (Why the hell would you think my servers are authoritative for those guys? (Or they may not care that my server is not a public recursive resolver like Cloudflare/Google are; they did a rudimentary port scan and found an open port 53, so it bluntly assumes this would be one of those guys.)) but also because it is an ANY-type query, which I have previously not paid any attention to (nor have the awareness of---I mean, there is TONS of DNS records I have never even heard of before: SSHFP, OPENPGPKEY, SVCB (not SRV!), HTTPS; and there's tons more deprecated. No way am I going to pay attention to all of them!) But ANY is a special type that literally means "return any record type"; a wildcard, if you will. And that's... not the best, yeah. (I mean I love it and would like that as an alternative to AXFR; but for the world? Especially when botnet tricks my server into dumping an entire zone on innocent IPs? No thanks...)
Fortunately, BIND9 has a config for that!
<https://bind9.readthedocs.io/en/stable/reference.html#namedconf-statement-minimal-any>
so before the attacker could figure out what zone I am really authoritative for and use that to attack, I can "disable" ANY queries... the issue is I haven't been able to get it working for the time being so I'll have to go figure that out now.

item.title: Markov-gibberish
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description: This isn't a site update. Still related, in the light of things. But anyway... So I gathered the motivation to update the Homebrew tap I have left untouched on Codeberg for months thanks to my next option to "ugh i don't have time now i'll try it in X months" being translated into "... you know what, I'll let Claude try it." (Under the impression that "fixing" something was going to take less time than writing something from the ground-up, but you don't have to tell me how wrong that belief was... (it's more of a motivation for myself, I should add! I feel more motivated to "do better" where I'm just pushing it just a bit harder, not committing it too much, not demanding for perfection; than get started from ground zero.)) But I got it working anyways! git-annex rclone-builtin special remote got a nice man page, and Homebrew was testing exactly what I wanted to test. (It's weird in places like not having explicit dependency on rclone 1.67.0+, but the test would have caught that; and I'm happy anyways.) So I pushed the collective work of Claude setting up the foundation and me dusting the corners, this time trying a different email to attribute Claude's code because I didn't quite like how it was a "no-reply" (could be a sign of something worse... maybe). But as I pushed I simultaneously wondered... what was Codeberg's stance on AI? Can I push this "AI-generated" code? "codeberg claude code"... I typed into Google. I saw this: <https://codeberg.org/ziglang/zig/!~codeberger~!.epochalen/fatalistischer-chenille%27s/duschend/Beherrschens/uneindeutigerer/> It hit me that I have seen things like this: barely bright dark background, QR code; gibberish that almost makes sense, wait... it looks like a scrambling of Git documentations? Later I learned this had to do with Markov-chain, but that's only AFTER the rabbit hole I went down, trying to pinpoint what this "advanced", going so far as to poison the very web itself... It's only recently that Codeberg used this rather neutral corpus for this gibberish generation though, and I can tell by how search engine bots like Googlebot being caught in the cross-fire. The index is still there, allowing me to see remnants of some of the more depressing, horrific text to ever exist: I looked up "Codeberg" with "was hopeless" (which, by the way, DON'T), and it was full of 1984. Something I have not read, but if even the gibberish GENERATED from it sounds so depressing, I don't know if I wish I had read the real thing to get the references (... no I don't.) It took me a few more searches to end up here: <https://lwn.net/Articles/1056953/> and it finally, FINALLY, gave me an answer: It's Iocaine. Named after a fictional, deadly poison... for this "Princess Bride" thing, I don't know. IT'S TERRIFYING. (Well, maybe for that part it mostly came from the corpus it generated from.) But no, it is actually the most unhinged thing I've ever seen: from the LWN and from myself testing it with curl(1), it examines your Sec-Fetch-* headers and sends you to jail if you don't send those headers; I have never once seen anything check if I'm really a browser this aggressively. The source code itself is a concoction of Rust, Nix, Lua, and a bunch of other languages I have never heard of or seen anything like the likes of: Fennel? (said to be Lisp syntax compiling to Lua; to me has an uncanny semblance of RUST with all the "fn"s (I'm not sure if Lua also uses "fn" please don't quote me on that)) Roto? (Rust but SCRIPT? My Vim syntax highlighter doesn't even recognize parse of the statements ToT) KDL? (okay maybe that comes from Caddy... MAYBE. Still unhinged though.) (at least it didn't try to stop me from cloning the repository, so... that's a good thing. I guess.) So let me get this straight: search engine crawlers ARE really caught in the middle of this cross-fire, MOST of which are well-behaved... like i'd say Google, or even Bingbot if I choose to let go of how deeply it crawled over my cgit instance (PetalBot being the exception though STOP BASHING YIZX.NET WITH THE **SAME** NONEXISTENT ROUTES, people like you have been doing that for like TWO years!!! Xc) But now (at least with the right search term), everywhere you look is this polluted nonsense, this digital wasteland. With only memories of what the Web once was to hold onto... and possibly not even that. It's sad... I don't want the Web to end up like this. I'd rather get hammered by PetalBot incessantly, even, if it meant that I could see my writing and everything I put up... somewhat unobstructed. This "deadliest poison" really lives up to its name, I can see... and that's also how I know that I won't be using it -- at least for now, not when my site has so little content it'd drown in this gibberish pile of words that I wouldn't even say to another person; that I could never. I don't mean to be dismissive... I know how relentless AI scrapers (read: badly written scrapers with the sole selfish intention of collecting data for training LLM) can be, as long as there is "gold" for them to mine. I'm just... too sad to think or act on this poison right now. At least Anubis felt defensive; this is an onslaught on humanity, the burning of the Library of Alexandria..... there has to be a better way right... we don't have to resort to "war".....

item.title: rdkw.org Zone (first-time hostmaster?)
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description: So I wanted to set up a page for rdkw.org to show a domain broker I've been in touch with (basically to show him a forwarded version of the email I sent to the Kuwaiti registrant of rdkw.net whose domain I've been vying for ever since I... well, thought of it could be a viable substitute for yizx.net for my family), and Gmail "shockingly" butchers my RFC822 attachment completely! Naturally I was going to change to an HTML part, until I remembered nobody actually opens an HTML file like a file. And that's when I had the idea of putting it on my web server, and giving him a link to it. ... which led me to signing keys with dnssec-ksr, publishing the DS hash on my registrar (Porkbun), and replacing the nameservers with my BIND9 servers.... (If you were wondering where that typo patch came from it was from me reading the DNSSEC tutorial on BIND9's ReadTheDocs... that's what I've been learning yeah :) It took a LOT of work (like, all the way from yesterday afternoon to midnight where I got tired, then 3 to 6am (when I woke up to see my roommate leave the balcony door open in the middle of a blizzard (granted I burnt my pizza leftover in the microwave causing an obscene amount of smoke in the living room but come on it's been hours since that happened!)), and 9am to now) but now having moved from Porkbun to my DNS servers I think it's working quite well! <https://dnsviz.net/d/git.rdkw.org/dnssec/> This Verisign validator also reminded me of how one (though it was the Ubuntu one, I'm not sure why?) of my servers wasn't reachable over IPv6 with UDP, so I also changed the YAML config in /etc/netplan on the Debian DO server by adding the IPv6 address and gateway... basically you can now reach it via IPv6. (I haven't been able to test IPv6 much from my laptop, so sorry to anyone who tried to connect over IPv6!) And yeah... if you look at the SOA record it'd say something like: ; <<>> DiG 9.20.20 <<>> @1.1.1.1 +multi SOA rdkw.org ; (1 server found) ;; global options: +cmd ;; Got answer: ;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 28639 ;; flags: qr rd ra ad; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 1 ;; OPT PSEUDOSECTION: ; EDNS: version: 0, flags:; udp: 1232 ;; QUESTION SECTION: ;rdkw.org. IN SOA ;; ANSWER SECTION: rdkw.org. 3600 IN SOA ns1.rapidcow.net. hostmaster.rapidcow.org. ( 1773771571 ; serial 43200 ; refresh (12 hours) 900 ; retry (15 minutes) 345600 ; expire (4 days) 7200 ; minimum (2 hours) ) (Note the "ad" (Authentic data) flag -- it means that Cloudflare approves of my DNSSEC signature! :) So I guess that makes me both the hostmaster and the webmaster now, eh? To some extent, though I don't plan to host my own DNS forever... deSEC and Cloudflare do a good enough job. The only thing I get annoyed at is that none of them let me upload my own zone file (well deSEC just straight up has no such interface (although it let me import the first time, I don't see any way to do it again? (Might try reverse-engineering what it did the first time, come to think of it... but anything I do from here is extra work and will only delay me working on homework that I was supposed to get started on this Saturday so nyah! Not doing that! >n<)) and Cloudflare... basically does not replace the existing records and panics at the sight of any duplicate entries, so what I've been doing is delete everything; re-import it (and PRAY that Cloudflare hasn't propagated its deletion); then delete any extraneous records like NS records at the apex (because at the moment I don't want Cloudflare to list me as secondary zones; I don't have any DS records delegating to my own keys so the trust chain will break if my servers were to act as authoritative for those servers (which they are, but also they don't sign anything... again KSK rollover will be exhausting, and I don't really want to commit to it until I get a taste of how it feels like for another few years...) Either way, that's all you really have to know! (Oh and of course I made DNS over HTTPS, that's a necessity to me -- though if you were to use it your queries would not be anonymous to me (BIND9 logs it), so just be careful with that... ;)

item.title: yizx.net DNS migration
item.author: webmaster@rapidcow.org
item.description:
Yeah something similar happened when over the weekend I decided I'm gonna do this migration to Cloudflare thing I said; this time I didn't forget any records but I did mis-recall which of my two VPSes actually runs www.YiZX.net. :x
Noticed this when I saw the UptimeRobot send me an email about "www.yizx.net DOWN", and because my sleepy ass only thought "why the hell not lol" and I anticipated less people to be affected by it (given that I've shared the site with at most two people and zero of them still talk to me to this day?), so I went to sleep first instead of fixing it the first thing after getting back from Cheesehacks lol
Sorry but I'm just trying to do things at my pace instead of pleasing non-existent "shareholders" in my "business". At this point I'm either out- sourcing my infrastructure for critical sites that people depend upon (just pub.rapidcow.org at this point; I am reclaiming the rapidcow.org for myself), or you're gonna have to put up with *my* sleep schedule :P (I really like the concept of a website that "sleeps", it makes my sleep sounder knowing my server isn't sucking energy out of the planet 24/7 (even if that is how VPSes work, I am considering moving them off because partly because I want to be physically reminded of the presence of a computer and the cost of keeping one alive.) I think taking a break occasionally is a healthy good promise that doesn't give way to the pressure that the tips they give about building an online profile and having an always-on always-connected server run under your name. (I just really don't like this idea about "everyone should build a web site because it costs you nothing" when you'd know damn well what it costs if you've ever looked at the physical power wattage it draws from your wall. And a web server that exists to serve nothing but a single page because the person who you have con- vinced to make a website is uninterested to update it might as well just be e-waste. Like, I don't know, you could say something similar for social media creating wasteful profiles, even go out as much length as creating bot accounts to make their platform look like people are using it. But for one we don't have to stoop that low in the first place simply because the Web is not social media, and for two... it's just wrong. Like why do you care that people do it if it's wrong. I'm not saying we should "gate-keep" website-making but for goodness sake we don't need every person, most of which uninterested in making a website on the Web; at least make them be aware of the cost, not just financially but real down-to-earth resource- wise costs. Sometimes I like to believe that the trouble exists because it forces you to think if the result is worth the cost, and having that cost forces you to evaluate if something is actually worth the cost.))
Anyways another idea I had is that I will be archiving past updates like these in /feed/<YEAR>/. I'm beginning to see that I've been (incorrectly) using this site as a weblog update thingy, and thought that archiving them as if they were one is pretty cool. I'll do that when I can get my hands on the Perl script I use to congregate these feed files (and when I get to actually formatting these into real HTML... :)
